wiki.title: Bögensee
wiki.description: High up in the Grey Mountains, the residents of Bögensee are isolated from the rest of the Reikland, close to the eerie ruins of Castle Drachenfels and the haunted stretches of the Grey Lady Pass. Sorrow and death are constant companions to those that live there. Recently, a great River Troll Hag named Grua Gribbleback has taken up residence downstream from the town, and is the latest in a line of monsters to bring tragedy to Bögensee’s inhabitants.

wiki.title: Helsee
wiki.description: Ice-cold and greasy to the touch, the waters of the lake known as Helsee are as black as a hangman's heart. The fork in the river mid-Stir offers a direct route to the northern shore of Helsee, and hence the mouth of the Vale of Darkness itself, without needing to risk open battle against the unliving. Furthermore, the river fork is unquestionably the fastest route from Altdorf to the vale.

wiki.title: Crystal Mere
wiki.description: Within Athel Loren, through the otherworldly waters of the Crystal Mere, Asrai prophetesses and scryers sift the strands of future fate, seeking significant signs or portents of the next threat.

wiki.title: Pools of Despair
wiki.description: The Pools of Despair are a phenomenon found within the lands of Nehekhara. It is unknown what foul magic spawned their creation, but as a collection of mirages, they have led many to their deaths. It is said that, as one's water supply runs short, a lush oasis will appear.

wiki.title: Cursed Marshes
wiki.description: Marienburg, the most infamous trading port in the Old World, lies in the midst of the stinking swampland called the Cursed Marshes. It is within these marshes that the Skaven Clan Scruten have their hidden stronghold, from where they launch their insidious raids beneath Marienburg and its surroundings. Around the year 2000 IC the clan was led away from Skavenblight by the Grey Seer Kritislik.

wiki.title: Middenland
wiki.description: Middenland, officially the Grand Duchies of Middenland and Middenheim, is a founding Electoral Province of the Empire that lies in the north-central region of that realm. Towering above the gloomy canopies of the Drakwald Forest is a sheer-sided pinnacle of white rock atop which sits the fortress city-state of Middenheim, capital of Middenland and the sacred City of the White Wolf. The White Wolf is the holy symbol of Ulric, the Imperial god of war, winter and wolves.

wiki.title: Bylorhof
wiki.description: Bylorhof is home to the worship of Bylorak, God of the Marshes, believed by some scholars to be an aspect of Taal or Manann. To the residents of this settlement, though, Bylorak is no scholar's aspect—he's their God, and they're proud to be his holiest site. When Vlad von Carstein began to drive the priests out of Sylvania, Bylorhof's priests of Sigmar, Shallya, and Morr all fled, but not the priest of Bylorak.

wiki.title: The Blight
wiki.description: The Blight is a large moorland within the Western Oblast region of Kislev that is mostly uninhabited. A few Kislevite tirsas dot the edge of the moors, making their living by mining peat, but the central regions have no known Human residents. The Blight is known to be home to monsters of various kinds, including Greenskins and Beastmen, as well as mutants.

wiki.title: Blighted Marshes
wiki.description: The Blighted Marshes, sometimes called the Blighted Marsh, the Zombie Swamps or the Zombie Marshes, and occasionally Putrid Swamp, is a swampy region that lies in north-western Tilea in the Principality of Tobaro, stretching from the River Trino to the Abasko Mountains. In their depths hide the Skaven and the capital of their Under-Empire, the subterranean city of Skavenblight. The Blighted Marshes are a lifeless area of shallow pools covered by a great swirling mist and fed by innumerable stinking streams.

wiki.title: Marshes of Madness
wiki.description: The Marshes of Madness are a swampland in the heart of the Badlands. During the days of great Nehekhara, this region was known as the Sinking Marshes of Khernarch. In the southern reaches of the dusty plains south of the Old World, the Blind River flows into a depression surrounded by a crescent of hills stretching from the Dragonback Mountains to the desert sands of Nehekhara.

wiki.title: Blood Marshes
wiki.description: The Blood Marshes are a vast, Chaos -corrupted wetland situated at the edge of the northern Chaos Wastes, along the coast of the Frozen Sea. The smell of death hangs heavily over this otherworldly wetland. In this place of murky water and seemingly innocuous animal life, blood chokes the waterways and beasts gorge themselves on the crimson ichor.

names.fr: Marais De La Glade Du Maudit

wiki.title: Swamp of Terror
wiki.description: Since the Great Necromancer commanded the waters of the Vitae River to be poisoned, its waters have become the colour of rotten blood, and its banks have become sickly and corrupted, populated only by the husks of deathless waterfowl, its floodplains stalked by great undead beasts. The Swamp of Terror lies within the domian of the Kings of Zandri.

wiki.title: Midden Moors
wiki.description: The Midden Moors, known locally as the Mirror Moors, are located in southwestern Middenland in the Empire. The meres of this moorland are still as glass, perfectly reflecting the night skies. Said to be haunted by the Ghosts of long-dead warriors, strange lights float among its mists, beckoning heedless travellers to follow, and rumours abound of a mysterious race of "Moorfolk" in the region known as Gnomes.

wiki.title: Hel Fenn
wiki.description: Hel Fenn is a legendary cursed swamp that lies at the northern lands of Sylvania, right along the banks of the River Stir. It is best known for being the site of the infamous Battle of Hel Fenn between the forces of the Empire of Man and the Vampire Count Mannfred von Carstein in 2145 IC that brought the Vampire Wars to an end. In ages past, the tribes of Men who scratched a living from these lands used to bury their dead in this swampland in the east of Sylvania.

wiki.title: Grootscher Marsh
wiki.description: The Grootscher Marsh is a large marshland located in the southwestern Empire at the convergence of the Reikland, Middenland, and the Wasteland. The marsh gained a cursed reputation among Imperial citizens when the Imperial Army lost the Battle of Grootscher Marsh in 2429 IC. This battle was one of the Empire's worst defeats in recent memory, and allowed the Wasteland and more importantly, the city-state of Marienburg, to secure its independence.

wiki.title: Uhland Bogs
wiki.description: The Uhland Bogs are a region of peat bogs along the Westerfluss, the river that forms the boundary between Reikland and The Wasteland. Many people from the surrounding villages harvest blocks of peat from the bogs and use them as fuel or ship them down to be sold along the Reik. Many standing stones, of significance to the Cult of Rhya, are located in the southwest portion of the peatland.

wiki.title: Reiker Marshes
wiki.description: Lying between the Reiker Heights and the Hohesesienen Hills at the sluggish confluence of the River Reik and the River Teufel, the Reiker Marshes are notoriously treacherous, and inexperienced captains frequently run aground in its deceptively shallow waters. Tattered flags and corroded signposts mark the most perilous sections, but these are woefully insufficient. River guides locally known as "huffers" are available to guide boats through the waters for a reasonable price, most of whom gather in the towns of Prieze and Babenborn on the Reik, and in significantly fewer numbers in Buxhead on the Teufel.

wiki.title: Bleak Moor
wiki.description: Bleak Moor is a large expanse of desolate land situated in north-eastern Albion. This treeless expanse is perpetually covered in a thick fog that is said to never lift. The landscape within the mist seems to change alarmingly, confusing travellers and making maps of the region useless.

names.fr: Baie De La Falaise De Craie

wiki.title: Dragon's Maw
wiki.description: The Dragon's Maw is a dangerous region of the Sea of Claws located north and west of the Gulf of L'Anguille off the Bretonnian coast. Any sailor with a semblance of sanity refuses to go anywhere near the region, as it has a deadly (and well-deserved) reputation, and only a very desperate or foolhardy captain would seek to navigate through the mist-shrouded waters of the Dragon's Maw. Dozens of sharp rocks rise from the water, and the tides and currents raise a constant spray from them, so that they look like teeth wreathed in smoke.

wiki.title: Mortis Tarn
wiki.description: The Mortis Tarn, known formerly as the Vitae Tarn is a large body of lakes situated high up within the Worlds Edge Mountains, forming the source of all the waters that flows through the now polluted Great Mortis River. When Nagash grew bitter over the resent of his own people, he polluted the source of all life within Nehekhara, the Vitae Tarn with large amount of Warpstone and Dark Magic, so much so that the waters began to look sickly and became the color of blood. Ever since then, the Tarn had been the source of the pollution that still runs across Nehekhara.

wiki.title: Black Water
wiki.description: In the Dwarf language, this vast lake is known as Varn Drazh, which means Black Water, and is the name by which it is known to Men. The lake is formed from a vast crater filled with the melt water of the surrounding mountains. In the ancient past, a meteor crashed from the sky to pound this huge gaping crater out of the rock.

wiki.title: Pirate's Current
wiki.description: The Pirate's Current, also spelled Pirates Current,{ or Pirates' Current, is a powerful and deadly sea current that flows through the strait between the island of Sartosa and the Tilean mainland to the north. It is one of the pirate city's most effective defences, especially against sea-borne assaults. The current is so dangerous that it makes it impossible for any ship to land on the north side of the island.

wiki.title: Golfo di Fodore
wiki.description: The Golfo di Fodore, also known as the Golfo di Forore, is a gulf of the north-western Tilean Sea embraced by the coasts of Tobaro and the Blighted Marshes.

wiki.title: Bay of Wrecks
wiki.description: The Bay of Wrecks separates the lands of Tilea from the Border Princes. It is part of the Lagoon of Tears. Though seemingly deep and tranquil, the waters of the Bay of Wrecks conceal jagged rocks that claim many vessels.

wiki.title: Straits of Lothern
wiki.description: The Straits of Lothern is the name given to the gap between the jagged fangs of rock that Lothern's Emerald and Sapphire Gates are built atop. Sandbars rise and fall throughout the channel in unpredictable ways, tides can change in a heartbeat whilst winds that had been gentle can become dangerously unpredictable squalls, dashing ships against the cliffs. All of this makes navigation hazardous for even the most experienced captains.

wiki.title: Middle Sea
wiki.description: Not to be confused with the Southern Sea. The Middle Sea is the stretch of the Great Ocean adjacent to the northern coast of Bretonnia in the Old World. It is surrounded by the Southern Sea to the south and by the Sea of Claws to the east.

wiki.title: Bitter Sea
wiki.description: The Bitter Sea, formally known as the Crystal Sea, is a body of water east of the Land of the Dead, north-east of Lybaras, and south from the Plain of Bones. To the north-west, it is connected by the Straits of Nagash to the polluted Sour Sea. The sea most likely got its name from the contaminated waters high up in the Worlds Edge Mountains, where the Sour Sea is located, its waters being polluted by huge amounts of warpstone that run off from the warpstone fragment that struck Cripple Peak many centuries ago, as well as the pollutants caused by the River Ruin that feeds into the Sea of Dread.

wiki.title: Sea of Dusk
wiki.description: The Sea of Dusk is one of two bodies of water that comprise the Inner Sea of Ulthuan. It breaks against the Bleak Coast, Caledor, Ellyrion, and western Avelorn. It also surrounds the Gaean Vale.

wiki.title: Sea of Dreams
wiki.description: The Sea of Dreams is one of the two masses of water comprising the Inner Sea of Ulthuan. As the eastern half, it surrounds the Island of Flame, and breaks against the coast of Saphery. It is also the first sea one enters when sailing inward from Lothern, Eataine.

wiki.title: Sea of Claws
wiki.description: The Sea of Claws is a bitterly cold and rough stretch of water that belongs to the Great Ocean, separating the northern Empire from the land of Norsca, and it has a well-deserved reputation as a hotbed of piracy. Of course pirates and foul weather don't stop dozens of ships sailing across it from Marienburg and other northern ports of the Old World, making it quite accessible for those wishing to cross it, either on their way to Norsca or other places further afield. Within the Sea of Claws lies the Dragon's Maw, also called the Dragon's Teeth, a jagged line of rocky islands off the northern tip of Bretonnia.

wiki.title: Tilean Sea
wiki.description: The Tilean Sea, also known as the Tilea Sea, is the warm and placid sea that separates the peninsula of Tilea from Estalia in the southern realms of the Old World. It is sometimes tempestuous, but only treacherous around the rocky islands of the coast south of Tobaro, and in the Pirates' Current. Apart from this, the sea is calm and easy sailing for small ships and sleek galleys.

wiki.title: Sea of Chaos
wiki.description: The Sea of Chaos is a Chaos -corrupted and near-frozen sea that forms a natural barrier between the northern peninsula of Norsca and the Chaos Wastes. It consists of the western region of the ocean adjacent to the Frozen Sea, which occupies the waters off Norsca's eastern coast. There are many reasons not to make the journey to the lands of the Norscans.

wiki.title: Sea of Dread
wiki.description: The Sea of Dread, also known as the Dread Sea, is a large body of water which lies south of the Darklands, east of the Southlands, and west of the Kingdoms of Ind. The Sea of Dread joins the Great Ocean at the southern tip of the Southlands and the Far Sea at the Gates of Calith. Within the Sea of Dread lie the Dragon Isles which are reputedly inhabited by Lizardmen who have turned feral without guidance from a Slann.

wiki.title: Sea of Chaos
wiki.description: The Sea of Chaos is a Chaos -corrupted and near-frozen sea that forms a natural barrier between the northern peninsula of Norsca and the Chaos Wastes. It consists of the western region of the ocean adjacent to the Frozen Sea, which occupies the waters off Norsca's eastern coast. There are many reasons not to make the journey to the lands of the Norscans.

wiki.title: The Grissenwald
wiki.description: The south-westernmost end of the Reikwald branches southwards along the Stirland border and thins out as it heads upriver towards the City-State of Nuln. This wide section of the forest is known locally as the Grissenwald, a tight woodland packed with distorted trees and twisted undergrowth, the depths of which are said to be swarming with Beastmen, Witches, and tribes of feral Mutants. Because of this, most local woodsmen travel in groups and seldom stay outdoors come nightfall, and its commonplace to find fluttering bills posted on roadside trees offering rewards for the retrieval of lost family and friends from the bowels of the forest.

wiki.title: Forest of Arden
wiki.description: The Forest of Arden spreads over the hinterland of Bretonnia and is a huge oak forest that extends up the slopes of the Grey Mountains. Because of this, it is often invaded by Orcs, Goblins and worse enemies descending from the higher peaks who pass into Bretonnia. In the depths of the forest they are able to hide and organise raids of the surrounding countryside.

wiki.title: Tettoverde Wood
wiki.description: Tettoverde Wood (meaning "greenroof" in the Tilean language ) is a forest located northern Tilea. Together with the Sussurrio Wood, the Tettoverde Wood is one of the biggest woodlands found on the peninsula. Tettoverde Wood is connected to the Worldroots of the Oak of Ages, providing an underground connection to the heart of the Wood Elves ' magical forest of Athel Loren.

wiki.title: Appentine Forest
wiki.description: The Appentine Forest is located at the edge of the Trantine Hills, near the city-state of Trantio in Tilea. In the scrub of this forest dwell fearsome Beastmen, who are always ready to attack the nearby settlements, such as when they assaulted Villa da Vincia. This forest is still reached by the Worldroots of the Oak of Ages, providing an underground connection to the heart of Athel Loren.

wiki.title: Bloodpine Woods
wiki.description: The Bloodpine Woods is a small forest located south of the Imperial capital at Altdorf. It is an outcrop of pine trees that grows down the southern face of the magical Amber Hills and spills into the depths of the Reikwald Forest. Called "bloodpine" for its deep-maroon wood, the lumber here is greatly desired by the artisans of Altdorf, and is most often used to produce exquisite furniture destined for the high-class markets of Marienburg and Nuln.

wiki.title: Dead Wood
wiki.description: Not to be confused with the Dead Wood found in north-western Naggaroth. Forming the southern border of Ostermark is a reputedly haunted forest known as the Dead Wood. The reason for its sinister reputation is that somewhere in its depths lie the ruins of Mordheim, a city so corrupted, so foul, Sigmar shattered it on the anvil of the earth.

wiki.title: Hunger Wood
wiki.description: Hunger Wood, also known as Verhungern is the most despised by the Sylvanian folk. It is a spirit -infested maze of briars and bogs, in which the unwary are easily trapped. Travellers that venture beneath the contorted boughs do not return.

wiki.title: Grim Wood
wiki.description: In the northeast of Sylvania is Grim Wood, which is haunted by an unseen monster that takes only maidens who dare to tread there.

wiki.title: Ghoul Wood
wiki.description: In the southern area of Sylvania is Ghoul Wood, said to be ruled by one of the Strigoi who has thrown in his lot with the Von Carsteins and lent them the aid of the flesh-eaters.

wiki.title: Forest of Châlons
wiki.description: The Forest of Châlons, also known as the Forest of Charons, is a crag-filled oaks forest close to the Massif Orcal. An altogether different forest from the other vast forests of Bretonnia, being located in the highlands west of the rocky crags of the Massif Orcal, the great, weather-beaten crags of rock that dominate the heartland of Bretonnia. The Forest of Châlons extends over rocky ravines, and crags and knolls of weathered rock reach above the stunted, gnarled trees.

wiki.title: Forest of Shadows
wiki.description: North and east of the Middle Mountains runs the Forest of Shadows. Shaped like an arm wrapped around the shoulders of the Middle Mountains, almost the whole of the province of Ostland is covered by the ominous Forest of Shadows. It earns its name, for it is the gloomiest of the Empire’s forests, its ancient trees having grown so close together that their branches nearly interweave like tightly clasped fingers.

wiki.title: Laurelorn Forest
wiki.description: Laurelorn Forest is a magical forest that lies on the northern coastline of the Empire of Man, home to reclusive communities of Eonir, a distinct community of Wood Elves. While both Middenland and Nordland claim the forest as theirs, the so-called "Wood Elves" dare either to try to enforce their claim. Laurelorn lies west of Salzenmund and the Silver Hills above it, and stretches west to the Imperial borders with the Wasteland.

wiki.title: Forest of Knives
wiki.description: The Forest of Knives is an ancient place, located deep in the frozen wilds the Norscan Peninsula, at the edge of the Chaos Wastes. The Winds of Magic blow hard there, corrupting all they touch.

wiki.title: Kharnos Forest
wiki.description: The Kharnos Forest is a dense woodland of the Border Princes on its border with Tilea, formed of mighty oaks that rises from the rugged shores of the Lagoon of Tears into the Apuccini Mountains of the south-western Border Princes. Long regarded as a lawless and dangerous region, the forest is infamous as a refuge for countless bandits, outlaws, smugglers and fugitives. The forest's name is likely derived either from " Karnos ", an ancient Classical name for Taal, the god of nature, still used in Tilea, and also employed in certain provinces of the Empire for his aspect as the Lord of Beasts, or from "Kharnos", the archaic name of the constellation later known as the Broken Cart.

wiki.title: Forest of Gloom
wiki.description: The Forest of Gloom is a forest located in the Border Princes near Black Fire Pass and Karaz-a-Karak, bordering the Black Mountains and Worlds Edge Mountains. The South Road, Old Dwarf Road, and Skull River run through it. The Forest of Gloom is one of the forests that collectively make up the thousand-mile-long belt of forest sometimes called the Black Deeps.

wiki.title: Piña Wood
wiki.description: Piña Wood is one of the two main forests of the Estalian peninsula, it is located in the realm of Obregon.

wiki.title: Sombra Wood
wiki.description: Sombra Wood is one of the two main forests of the Estalian peninsula. It is located in the Kingdom of Cantonia in south-eastern Estalia, just south of the eastern stretch of the Irrana Mountains.

wiki.title: Sussurrio Wood
wiki.description: Sussurrio Wood (meaning something like "wood of whispers" in the Tilean language ) is a forest in southern Tilea. Together with the Tettoverde Wood the Sussurrio Wood is one of the biggest woodlands found on the peninsula. Sussurrio Wood is connected to the Worldroots of the Oak of Ages, providing an underground connection to the heart of the Wood Elves ' magical forest of Athel Loren.

wiki.title: Notnam Forest
wiki.description: Notnam Forest is a small Wood Elf land ruled by King Rollo Tripleg. Normally Rollo would not have crossed the borders of his kingdom, as defined by the river Trentuin, for anything. Anything, that is, except money; realising this Aer Dressair made suitable overtures and persuaded the aging monarch from his silvan haunt.

wiki.title: Middle Mountains
wiki.description: The Middle Mountains, called Mitteberge in Reikspiel, are a desolate mountain range located in the north-western region of the Empire, which acts as a natural border for the lands of Nordland, Ostland, Hochland and Middenland. This range of mountains is notorious for being highly devoid of valuable resources and mineral deposits, to such an extent that the Dwarfs who had previously colonised the mountains have all but abandoned them and returned to the domains of the more resource-rich Worlds Edge Mountains. Nonetheless, this range of mountains has in the past provided adequate shelter for the Empire's people, resulting in the creation of cities such as Middenheim and Wolfenburg.

wiki.title: The Vaults
wiki.description: Not to be confused with the Grey Vaults. The Vaults are a mountainous region of the Old World consisting of deep, ice-cut valleys, frozen glaciers and towering peaks that form the junction between the Black Mountains and the Grey Mountains. Its immense mountains geographically divide the lands of Tilea, Bretonnia, the Empire and the Border Princes.

wiki.title: Massif Orcal
wiki.description: The sheer cliffs of the Massif Orcal rise above the wild Forest of Châlons in Bretonnia and mark the beginning of a rocky highland occupied by Greenskins and other monsters. The Massif Orcal is a barren, desolate place, a blighted region almost devoid of life. Scraggly pines cling to some of the upper heights, and equally sickly-looking brambles creep about the lower slopes, vainly trying to wrest moisture from the thin layer of soil that powders the rocks.

wiki.title: Grey Mountains
wiki.description: The Grey Mountains, called the Arluii by the Elves, are the mountain range forming the border between the Empire of Man to the east and Bretonnia and the Forest of Loren to the west, and these peaks are mainly inhabited by Grey Dwarfs and Human mountaineers. The range stretches out from the Vaults in the south to the Pale Sisters in the north close to the Sea of Claws. One pass bridges it, Axe Bite Pass, which is guarded by many fortresses, such as Castle Montfort, and ends close to the great city of Parravon on the Bretonnian side while it is flanked on the other side of the border by the stout Imperial fortified town of Helmgart in Reikland.

wiki.title: Grey Mountains
wiki.description: The Grey Mountains, called the Arluii by the Elves, are the mountain range forming the border between the Empire of Man to the east and Bretonnia and the Forest of Loren to the west, and these peaks are mainly inhabited by Grey Dwarfs and Human mountaineers. The range stretches out from the Vaults in the south to the Pale Sisters in the north close to the Sea of Claws. One pass bridges it, Axe Bite Pass, which is guarded by many fortresses, such as Castle Montfort, and ends close to the great city of Parravon on the Bretonnian side while it is flanked on the other side of the border by the stout Imperial fortified town of Helmgart in Reikland.

wiki.title: Black Mountains
wiki.description: The Black Mountains divide the territory of the Empire of Man from the wild, southern lands of the Border Princes. The skies above this range are wreathed in black thunderheads and flocks of Blood Harpies, while Ice Giants and other predatory creatures prowl the blizzard-swept slopes. The Black Mountains are riddled with crude, Goblin -hewn tunnels and infested with all manner of ravenous beasts, including Trolls, Wyverns and dreaded Cockatrices.

wiki.title: Worlds Edge Mountains
wiki.description: The Worlds Edge Mountains, also spelled World's Edge Mountains and sometimes called the " Mountains-at-World's-End " and Saraeluii (lit. "Mountains at the Edge of the World") in Eltharin, the language of the Elves, is the longest mountain range in the Known World and one of the highest. Stretching from the northern Chaos Wastes and extending southwards across the eastern Old World into the Southlands, they form a natural barrier between the Old World and the Dark Lands of the Far East. The Worlds Edge Mountains were at the heart of the great Dwarf empire of Karaz Ankor in ancient days, and even now, many great Dwarf Holds and fortresses may be found amidst this towering range of peaks.

names.fr: Montagnes Du Bord Du Monde Nordique

wiki.title: Worlds Edge Mountains
wiki.description: The Worlds Edge Mountains, also spelled World's Edge Mountains and sometimes called the " Mountains-at-World's-End " and Saraeluii (lit. "Mountains at the Edge of the World") in Eltharin, the language of the Elves, is the longest mountain range in the Known World and one of the highest. Stretching from the northern Chaos Wastes and extending southwards across the eastern Old World into the Southlands, they form a natural barrier between the Old World and the Dark Lands of the Far East. The Worlds Edge Mountains were at the heart of the great Dwarf empire of Karaz Ankor in ancient days, and even now, many great Dwarf Holds and fortresses may be found amidst this towering range of peaks.

names.fr: Montagnes Du Bord Du Monde Sud

wiki.title: Apuccini Mountains
wiki.description: The Apuccini Mountains, also called the Apuccinis,, Appuccinis,, Appucinis, or Puccini Mountains, divide the lands of eastern Tilea from the Border Princes. They are generally avoided by Human travellers, since there are numerous bandit strongholds, Goblin caves and the dwellings of other evil creatures. The mountains are thickly wooded along both their eastern and western slopes, and there are no Dwarf populations within them as far as is known.

wiki.title: Abasko Mountains
wiki.description: The Abasko Mountains form the border between Tilea and Estalia, spreading northwards till they connect with the Irrana Mountains. Vast veins of silver are mined by Estalia within the Abasko, which, alongside a rich agricultural industry, maintains their strong economy. The slopes of the Abasko Mountains are renowned for their pale wood, used to craft fine furniture.

wiki.title: Irrana Mountains
wiki.description: The Irrana Mountains are the range of mountains in the southern Old World that divide Tilea from the lands of Bretonnia and Estalia. It is colloquially subdivided into two mountainous sub-regions, the Eastern Irrana Mountains and Western Irrana Mountains. Bretonnians often just call them both the Southern Mountains.

wiki.title: Irrana Mountains
wiki.description: The Irrana Mountains are the range of mountains in the southern Old World that divide Tilea from the lands of Bretonnia and Estalia. It is colloquially subdivided into two mountainous sub-regions, the Eastern Irrana Mountains and Western Irrana Mountains. Bretonnians often just call them both the Southern Mountains.

wiki.title: Vanaheim Mountains
wiki.description: The soaring Vanaheim Mountains of Norsca are capped with snow year round, their frozen peaks home to many monstrous beasts that are often hunted by the Norscan tribes for their meat and fur.

names.fr: Montagnes Du Bord Du Monde Nordique

wiki.title: Dragonback Mountains
wiki.description: The Dragonback Mountains are a range of mountains located within the eastern shores of the Black Gulf, adjacent to the Worlds Edge Mountains in the East, and comprising much of the Badlands western borders. Dragonback in ancient times was a Dwarf Hold in its own right, first founded by an expedition of the Angbok Clan but it was the Rinkeldraz Clan who would later become the Kings of Dragonback. However, following the onset of the Goblin Wars, the Mines of Ekrund and the whole Dragonback Mountains range have since fallen to the marauding Greenskin tribes that invaded the Badlands in -1500 IC.

wiki.title: Iron Mountains
wiki.description: The Iron Mountains are a mountain range in north-western Naggaroth, between the Boiling Sea and the Sea of Malice. The great Dark Elf city of Naggarond lies in the eastern foothills. Dark Pegasi notably nest within these mountains.

wiki.title: Beast Peaks
wiki.description: The Beast Peaks are a clump of mountains deep in the interior of the isle of Albion. Their heights are enshrouded in low cloud, obscured by constant rain and storm, so that the actual size of the mountains is unknown. They are known as the "Beast Peaks" due to the high number of monstrous creatures that live in these mountains, whether they live in the high altitudes above the cloud-line, or within the innumerable caves and labyrinthine caverns that riddle the mountains like honey-comb.

wiki.title: Atalan Mountains
wiki.description: The Atalan Mountains is a range of mountains found in north-west Araby. The land of Araby lies along the north-west coast of the Southlands, between the Atalan Mountains and the Great Ocean. To the east is the Great Desert of Araby that separates Araby from the Land of the Dead.

names.fr: Montagnes Du Bord Du Monde Sud

wiki.title: Grey Mountains
wiki.description: The Grey Mountains, called the Arluii by the Elves, are the mountain range forming the border between the Empire of Man to the east and Bretonnia and the Forest of Loren to the west, and these peaks are mainly inhabited by Grey Dwarfs and Human mountaineers. The range stretches out from the Vaults in the south to the Pale Sisters in the north close to the Sea of Claws. One pass bridges it, Axe Bite Pass, which is guarded by many fortresses, such as Castle Montfort, and ends close to the great city of Parravon on the Bretonnian side while it is flanked on the other side of the border by the stout Imperial fortified town of Helmgart in Reikland.

wiki.title: Peak Pass
wiki.description: Peak Pass runs through the Worlds Edge Mountains. It connects the Dark Lands with the Imperial Great Province of Ostermark. During the Golden Age, the Dwarfs fortified the pass, which connects to the great Dwarf hold of Karak Kadrin ("Stronghold of the Pass" in Khazalid ).

wiki.title: High Pass
wiki.description: High Pass (called Belyerovota Pass in Kislevarin ) is the northernmost pass over the Worlds Edge Mountains and certainly the most treacherous. It connects Kislev with the Great Skull Land.

wiki.title: Black Fire Pass
wiki.description: Black Fire Pass, or Haz Drazh Kadrin as it is known in Khazalid, lies in the southeastern Empire of Man in the Electoral Province of Averland. Formed long ago when violent eruptions tore the Black Mountains in two, the pass is a gaping chasm of contorted lava flanked by steep black cliffs of polished volcanic glass. Eerie wisps of black vapour gush from vents at the base of the crags to form surging shapes against the darkened rock.

wiki.title: The Vaults
wiki.description: Not to be confused with the Grey Vaults. The Vaults are a mountainous region of the Old World consisting of deep, ice-cut valleys, frozen glaciers and towering peaks that form the junction between the Black Mountains and the Grey Mountains. Its immense mountains geographically divide the lands of Tilea, Bretonnia, the Empire and the Border Princes.

wiki.title: The Vaults
wiki.description: Not to be confused with the Grey Vaults. The Vaults are a mountainous region of the Old World consisting of deep, ice-cut valleys, frozen glaciers and towering peaks that form the junction between the Black Mountains and the Grey Mountains. Its immense mountains geographically divide the lands of Tilea, Bretonnia, the Empire and the Border Princes.

wiki.title: Apuccini Mountains
wiki.description: The Apuccini Mountains, also called the Apuccinis,, Appuccinis,, Appucinis, or Puccini Mountains, divide the lands of eastern Tilea from the Border Princes. They are generally avoided by Human travellers, since there are numerous bandit strongholds, Goblin caves and the dwellings of other evil creatures. The mountains are thickly wooded along both their eastern and western slopes, and there are no Dwarf populations within them as far as is known.

wiki.title: Mad Dog Pass
wiki.description: Mad Dog Pass, called Varag Kadrin in the Dwarf tongue of Khazalid, cuts through the Worlds Edge Mountains between two branches of the Howling River, north of Barak Varr and the Blood River. Of the three passes through the mountains, it is the one most accessible from the Border Princes -- the Silver Road connects to the Old Dwarf Road that runs through the Forest of Gloom and from there merges with the Black Fire Pass of the Black Mountains, while Death Pass leads into the Badlands well below the protective line of the Blood River. Because of this, Mad Dog Pass has become a major thoroughfare and is the route of choice for anyone travelling from the Border Princes to the Dark Lands and back again.

wiki.title: Death Pass
wiki.description: Death Pass is a pass through the Worlds Edge Mountains from the Old World to the Dark Lands of the Far East. It is occupied on both sides by the Broken Tooth Orc tribe. It passes near Black Crag, a lost Dwarf hold formerly known as Karak Drazh.

names.fr: Col De La Morsure De La Hache

wiki.title: Gisoreux Gap
wiki.description: The Gisoreux Gap is one of only three locations within the entire Grey Mountains that allow passage between Bretonnia and the Empire, connecting the Duchy of Gisoreux with the Imperial state of Reikland.

wiki.title: Irrana Mountains
wiki.description: The Irrana Mountains are the range of mountains in the southern Old World that divide Tilea from the lands of Bretonnia and Estalia. It is colloquially subdivided into two mountainous sub-regions, the Eastern Irrana Mountains and Western Irrana Mountains. Bretonnians often just call them both the Southern Mountains.

wiki.title: Abasko Mountains
wiki.description: The Abasko Mountains form the border between Tilea and Estalia, spreading northwards till they connect with the Irrana Mountains. Vast veins of silver are mined by Estalia within the Abasko, which, alongside a rich agricultural industry, maintains their strong economy. The slopes of the Abasko Mountains are renowned for their pale wood, used to craft fine furniture.

wiki.title: Prie Ridge
wiki.description: Prie Ridge is a scree-laden highland near the center of the Skaag Hills. Although there are many abandoned mines in it, almost nobody visits the area today. It's just these qualities that, according to the dockers of the nearby town of Prie, make it an ideal place to dispose of bodies.

wiki.title: Zamak Spayenya
wiki.description: Zamak Spayenya is a great white rock, a league or more across, rising from the steppe. Its top is almost flat, and its sides are very steep, making it a useful temporary redoubt. The limestone contains caves, many of which are decorated with paintings dating back centuries; the place was sacred once.

wiki.title: Barren Hills
wiki.description: The Barren Hills of western Talabecland are widely considered to be cursed. Old folktales speak of a time when they were called the Green Hills, which many believe refers to a time before any curse fell upon them. Among the elders of certain nearby settlements, however, it is claimed that the name is derived from the odd colour the hills glow on ill-omened nights.

wiki.title: Skaag Hills
wiki.description: The rocky Skaag Hills lie to the west of the River Bögen and run along the southern bank of the Reik before falling beneath the trees of the Duchy of Gorland. Near the centre, the Reikwald recedes from the stony crags and layers of stratified rock rise to the scree-laden highlands of the Prie Ridge. A single road crosses the gentler slopes of the Skaag Hills to the south, starting at Trosreut in the shadow of Castle Grauenberg and wending its way through to Holthausen, but many minor tracks and trails also cross the region, most of which started as goat tracks.

wiki.title: Hägercrybs
wiki.description: The Hägercrybs are a range of heavily forested hills in central Reikland, stretching from the Princedom of Altdorf to the Freistadt of Ubersreik. So rugged are they that no road runs through them east to west, a major inconvenience for many travellers. They are mainly used by men for sheep-herding, and many shepherds live throughout the hills.

wiki.title: Greenleaf
wiki.description: The Greenleaf is a county located in the south-east Mootland, once known as the Duchy of Fallow Hills. The county is named after the Greenleaf Hills, with its inhabitants often calling themselves "Greenleafers", as a way to distinguish their sense of independence from the greater Mootland. Due to a cartographical error in the creation of the Mootland, there was one tiny part of the Empire owned by no Electoral Province.

wiki.title: Barrows of Cuileux
wiki.description: The Barrows of Cuileux should not be confused with the Grave of Cuileux. The Grave is the site of the last battle between the Knights of Cuileux and the Greenskin horde. The Barrows of Cuileux are where the Cuilen buried their dead.

wiki.title: Weiss Hills
wiki.description: The Weiss Hills is a sparsely inhabited area of moorlands and low hills that lies deep within the forests of Hochland. The region is mainly travelled by poachers and licensed trappers and hunters. Much of the land is a royal demesne of the Elector Count of Hochland, watched over by the Warden of Fort Schippel.

wiki.title: Howling Hills
wiki.description: The Howling Hills are a ridge of craggy peaks that sweep from Middenheim at their western-most extent almost to Talabheim to their east. The tallest of the hills are bare and rocky, their plateaus an endless series of sodden moors covered in heather and coarse grasses, lending them a desolate aspect, while the lower ranges and deep valleys are wooded with dense and rainswept forest. The Howling Hills were considered to be part of Hochland during the Skaven Wars of the twelfth century IC, yet are now part of Middenland according to maps of the 26th century IC.

wiki.title: Trantine Hills
wiki.description: Beyond the walls of Trantio in Tilea, lies Trantine Hills rich of fruit orchards and olive groves around Trantio. The hills are also well known for the many battles fought by Trantio against Pavona or other city-state and Bretonnia. Many abandoned villas dot the countryside hills above Trantio, as in safer and more prosperous times it had been the fashion among the city's wealthy merchant families to build such palaces in the surrounding countryside, both as an ostentatious display of wealth and as a retreat from squalor. city.

wiki.title: Osso Hills
wiki.description: The Osso Hills are a region of hills in the hinterland of the island of Sartosa.

wiki.title: Bone Hills
wiki.description: The Bone Hills are an arid region of Estalia infamous as the home of witch -cursed Skin Wolf clans and the Strega of the Bone Hills.

wiki.title: Céfiro Hills
wiki.description: The Céfiro Hills are a group of hills located in the Estalian Kingdom of Obregon.

wiki.title: Feroz Hills
wiki.description: The Feroz Hills are a group of hills located in the Estalian Kingdom of Bilbali. The hills can be reached by a Skaven tunnel of the Under-Empire which leads from the ratmen 's lair of Gnaw Pit.

wiki.title: Miramar Hills
wiki.description: The Miramar Hills are a group of hills in the Estalian Kingdom of Avila.

wiki.title: Geistenmund Hills
wiki.description: The Geistenmund Hills are home to ancient barrows where some long-forgotten people were purportedly laid to rest. Centuries ago, Necromancers exiled from Bretonnia settled in the region and used their magics to raise the dead from the barrows with powerful runes, wards, and stone arches. These protections have grown old, however, and occasionally, someone will destroy the runes to free the restless dead.

wiki.title: Varenka Hills
wiki.description: Dotted with ancient burial mounds, the Varenka Hills are a haunted place, shunned by those who dwell in the frontier towns that cluster along the banks of the nearby rivers. The Varenka Hills are where the Skull River flows into the Black Gulf, against the lands of the Border Princes. Some Dawi in other holds claim this gives the Dwarfs of Barak Varr a strange outlook, more Manling than Dwarf.

wiki.title: Broken Spine
wiki.description: The peaks of the Broken Spine are but foothills in comparison to the Worlds Edge Mountains, but they form no less a barrier to evil. Without them, the eldritch winds that blow through Sylvania would carry armies of the dead further into Stirland, the Moot, and perhaps even across Aver Reach. As it is, the fell winds are contained by this hinterland, and many powerful Undead with them.

wiki.title: Wyvern Cliffs
wiki.description: Even to those that have no knowledge of events that gave the Wyvern Cliffs their name, it is perhaps unsurprising to any who learn that there was indeed a wyvern involved and, yes, there was a slaughter. When one delves a little deeper into the history of that sorry event, it all came about when a sneaky Goblin, Furgit Gutslasha, tried to impress his Orc overlord by climbing Iron Rock and make off with a wyvern hatchling to present as a gift to his master. Suffice to say that the maternally outraged mother was not impressed, and proceeded to annihilate the entire greenskin tribe.

wiki.title: Teufeltal
wiki.description: The Teufeltal ("Devil's Valley") is a bowl of a valley surrounded on all sides by the high land of the Grey Mountains. Its scrubby hillsides are suitable for little other than sheep farming, though there are a few vineyards around Tallerhof. The Teufel itself flows from beneath the great mountain Frugelhorn and settles in a high lake.

wiki.title: Luccini
wiki.description: Luccini, also spelled Lucini, officially the Ancient Principality of Luccini, is considered the oldest city in Tilea, at least according to the people that live there. Founded upon the ruins of an ancient High Elven city in the year 1 IC, by the legendary twins, Lucan and Luccina, king and queen of a tribe of nomadic shepherds who settled on the famous Elf -built Acropolis and built their palace at its summit. No wonder that the name of the city itself is taken from that of its first queen.

wiki.title: Plain of Bones
wiki.description: The Plain of Bones is a desert land, despoiled by windblown pollutants carried from the furnaces and factories of the Chaos Dwarf empire and ravaged by centuries of abuse by wandering tribes of Orcs and Goblins. The northern and eastern edges of this awful place about the empire of the Chaos Dwarfs where the dread Tower of Gorgoth looks out over the Desolation of Azgorh. The southern boundary lies on beaches of poisoned land along the shores of the Sea of Dread.

names.fr: Champ De Glace De Drergen Mort

wiki.title: Vale of Darkness
wiki.description: This article is a stub. You can help Warhammer Wiki by expanding it. The Vale of Darkness feeds the Lake Helsee with Castle Templehof to the East and the Falls of Despair to it's West.

wiki.description: Not to be confused with the Grey Vaults. The Vaults are a mountainous region of the Old World consisting of deep, ice-cut valleys, frozen glaciers and towering peaks that form the junction between the Black Mountains and the Grey Mountains. Its immense mountains geographically divide the lands of Tilea, Bretonnia, the Empire and the Border Princes.

wiki.title: Sonnental
wiki.description: In the northern Border Princes, in the shadow of the haunted Geistenmund Hills, lies the town of Sonnental. Originally founded by Imperial exiles, Sonnental now has a darker heritage. The town's walls are guarded by the Undead, not only to keep the marauders and Greenskins out, but also to keep the inhabitants in.
